feature: Canonical Unicode dictionary hyphenation with original source offsets
regression_before_fix: The canonical-accent test failed at its Portuguese decomposed-word hyphenation assertion before normalization was implemented.
assertions: Composed and decomposed Portuguese, German and French have equal normalized line text and automatic hyphen decisions
Original source bytes are covered without gaps
Breaks remain at source grapheme boundaries
Glyph clusters retain valid original source offsets
Resumed page bounds and raster output equal eager pagination
Existing CSS restrictions, soft hyphens, unsupported languages and oversized-word checks pass
implementation: NFC per grapheme for non-ASCII dictionary lookup, with normalized-end to original-byte mapping; ASCII borrows the source. Existing unicode-normalization 0.1.26 is reused.
limits: 128 original source bytes per dictionary word
At most 128 grapheme offset pairs per lookup
Alphabetic-character check after NFC; noncomposing nonalphabetic marks still skip dictionary lookup
Equivalent spellings across the source-byte limit may differ
commands: nix-shell --run 'cargo fmt --all && cargo test --locked -p femto-reader && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features desktop,femto-catalog/tailnet --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check'

firmware_manifest.installation_status: No automatic installer. Verify the actual device partition table and recovery backup before installation.

limitations: No new full workspace test suite or native simulator run
Physical text quality and memory peaks remain unqualified
